                                  1          Plaintiff Dr. Andrei Gafita (“Gafita”) brings this action against Defendants Nucs AI, Inc.

                                  2   (“Nucs AI”), Nijat Ahmadov (“Ahmadov”), and Farid Yagubbayli (“Yagubbayli”) and alleges

                                  3   as follows:

                                  4                                          INTRODUCTION

                                  5          1.       Dr. Andrei Gafita brings this action against Nucs AI to enforce his entitlement to

                                  6   the substantial equity stake he was promised in exchange for his highly valuable ideas and

                                  7   intellectual property that constitute the core technology underlying Nucs AI’s products, his

                                  8   business plan, and access to his professional network.

                                  9          2.       Gafita is a respected and accomplished doctor and medical researcher currently

                                 10   practicing at Johns Hopkins Medicine. In 2023, Gafita developed the seed of a new technology

                                 11   that could revolutionize the diagnosis and treatment of prostate cancer using artificial
550 CALIFORNIA ST., SUITE 1040
  SAN FRANCISCO, CA 94104




                                 12   intelligence.
     GRELLAS SHAH LLP




                                 13          3.       Gafita agreed to work with Farid Yagubbayli to develop his ideas into a

                                 14   marketable product. Yagubbayli introduced Gafita to his friend Nijat Ahmadov, and together

                                 15   the three agreed to start Nucs AI.

                                 16          4.       In recognition of his substantial contributions at the enterprise’s outset—without

                                 17   which Nucs AI could never have existed—Ahmadov and Yagubbayli agreed to issue Gafita

                                 18   4,700,000 shares of common stock in the new company. Unlike Ahmadov and Yagubbayli’s

                                 19   own shares, Gafita’s would not be subject to vesting but would be issued in full upon Nucs AI’s

                                 20   formation.

                                 21          5.       But no sooner had Gafita received his shares than Ahmadov and Yagubbayli

                                 22   began working to undermine his ability to realize his ownership of them. At first falsely claiming

                                 23   it was necessary to secure initial investment, then falsely claiming it reflected the limited hours

                                 24   Gafita could contribute to daily operations at Nucs AI, and then again that it was necessary to

                                 25   secure additional investment, Ahmadov and Yagubbayli coerced Gafita into signing

                                 26   amendments to his stock purchase agreement that resulted in his shares first partially and then

                                 27   fully revesting. All this time, Ahmadov and Yagubbayli assured Gafita that he was a critical

                                 28   member of the Nucs AI team and would be compensated for his contributions, including with a

                                                                                        1

                                  1   seat on the board of directors. These reassurances were all false and intended to convince Gafita

                                  2   to sign away his right to his shares.

                                  3          6.      When Gafita confronted Ahmadov about the unfairness of his revesting

                                  4   agreements, Ahmadov and Yagubbayli began engineering a pretextual scheme to remove Gafita

                                  5   from the company. Ahmadov told Gafita that the Board of Directors was determined to terminate

                                  6   his consulting agreement immediately, and offered him the choice to either step down and

                                  7   relinquish most of his shares, or agree to a reduced role and vastly reduced equity share. But,

                                  8   unfortunately for defendants, Gafita and Nucs AI had a written agreement that if Gafita was

                                  9   terminated without cause his shares would immediately vest in full. To avoid this outcome,

                                 10   Ahmadov and Yagubbayli constructed a set of false and pretextual bases to terminate Gafita for

                                 11   “cause,” which would allow Nucs AI to repurchase Gafita’s shares for a fraction of their value.

                                  1                                           JURISDICTION

                                  2          12.     This Court has original jurisdiction over this action under 28 U.S.C. § 1332

                                  3   because the amount in controversy exceeds the value of $75,000 and because this dispute is

                                  4   between Gafita, a citizen of Maryland, Nucs AI, a citizen of Delaware and/or California or New

                                  5   York, and Ahmadov and Yagubbayli, both foreign citizens.

                                  6          13.     Defendant Nucs AI is subject to personal jurisdiction in the State of California

                                  7   because it submitted and consented to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state of California in the

                                  8   First and Second Amendments to the Common Stock Purchase Agreement between Gafita and

                                  9   Nucs AI, attached as Exhibit B and Exhibit C to this Complaint, and agreed that any litigation

                                 10   arising from said agreements shall be conducted only in the courts of California or the federal

                                 11   courts of the United States located in California and no other courts.
550 CALIFORNIA ST., SUITE 1040
  SAN FRANCISCO, CA 94104




                                 12          14.     Defendants Ahmadov and Yagubbayli are subject to personal jurisdiction in the
     GRELLAS SHAH LLP




                                 13   State of California because they purposely availed themselves of California, and San Francisco

                                 14   specifically, by representing Nucs AI as having a presence in San Francisco on its website and

                                 15   LinkedIn profile, and by including a San Francisco mailing address on their Nucs AI email

                                 16   signature blocks. Ahmadov and Yagubbayli invoked the status and prestige of a San Francisco

                                 17   address for a technology start-up company to raise the profile of Nucs AI and themselves, and

                                 18   the majority of acts alleged in this complaint occurred while Nucs AI, Ahmadov, and

                                 19   Yagubbayli were deliberately creating an impression that they were present in the State of

                                 20   California and the City of San Francisco. Gafita’s claims against Ahmadov and Yagubbayli arise

                                 21   out of his contacts with the forum state, namely, the fraudulent representations they made to

                                 22   Gafita were intended to induce his continued contracting and provision of services for a

                                 23   California entity, and Ahmadov and Yagubbayli were holding themselves out as situated in

                                 24   California at the time they made the fraudulent representations.

                                 27   Nucs AI consented to a California forum and its primary place of business is or was within this

                                 28   district. Furthermore, a substantial part of the breach of the contract and tortious conduct alleged

                                 27   Board resolved that 100% of the shares issued to Ahmadov and Yagubbayli were subject to

                                                                                       4
